dhp44:2:
& this realm of death
with all its gods?
dhp44:3:
Who will ferret out
the well-taught Dhamma-saying,
dhp44:4:
as the skillful flower-arranger
the flower?
dhp45:1:
The learner-on-the-path
will penetrate this earth
dhp45:2:
& this realm of death
with all its gods.
dhp45:3:
The learner-on-the-path
will ferret out
the well-taught Dhamma-saying,
dhp45:4:
as the skillful flower-arranger
the flower.
dhp46:1:
Knowing this body
is like foam,
dhp46:3:
cutting out
the blossoms of Mara,
dhp46:4:
you go where the King of Death
can’t see.
The man immersed in
gathering blossoms,
his heart distracted:
dhp47:3:
as a great flood,
a village asleep.
dhp48:4:
his heart distracted,
insatiable in sensual pleasures:
the End-Maker holds him
under his sway.
dhp49:1:
As a bee–without harming
the blossom,
its color,
its fragrance–
takes its nectar & flies away:
dhp49:4:
so should the sage
go through a village.
dhp50:1:
Focus,
not on the rudenesses of others,
dhp50:2:
not on what they’ve done
or left undone,
dhp50:3:
but on what you
have & haven’t done
yourself.
dhp53:1:
Just as from a heap of flowers
many garland strands can be made,
dhp53:3:
one born & mortal
should do
–with what’s born & is mortal–
dhp54:1:
No flower’s scent
goes against the wind–
dhp54:3:
But the scent of the good
does go against the wind.
dhp54:4:
The person of integrity
wafts a scent
in every direction.
dhp55:4:
among these scents,
the scent of virtue
is unsurpassed.
dhp56:3: while the scent of virtuous conduct
dhp58:1: As in a pile of rubbish
dhp58:2: cast by the side of a highway
dhp59:1: so in the midst of the rubbish-like,
dhp59:4:
the disciple of the Rightly
Self-Awakened One.
